headline: US State Department approves possible $2.1bn sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 MSE interceptors to Ukraine, funded entirely by allies
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- approval] The State Department approved a possible Foreign Military Sale to Ukraine of 500 PATRIOT PAC-3 MSE missiles and related equipment, estimated $2.1 billion, Lockheed Martin principal contractor; Ukraine requested 500 missiles plus classified/unclassified spare parts and…
sources: US State Department, Bureau of Political-Military Affairs (Foreign Military Sales: Congressional Notification); Reuters (Mike Stone, Andrea Shalal, Tom Balmforth); Volodymyr Zelenskyy (X, late Friday, via Firstpost)
fault_line: Relief or IOU? An approval Kyiv waited a month for -- but the missiles are not built yet, allies pay, and Congress still reviews: does this deter tonight's ballistic wave, or just promise the 2030s?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- approval] The State Department approved a possible Foreign Military Sale to Ukraine of 500 PATRIOT PAC-3 MSE missiles and related equipment, estimated $2.1 billion, Lockheed Martin principal contractor; Ukraine requested 500 missiles plus classified/unclassified spare parts and logistics/software support. [VERIFIED FACT -- funding] 'Funded entirely by partners and allies': Ukraine pays with donations from Canada, Germany and Norway via the US JUMPSTART programme plus national funds financed by the EU Ukraine Support Loan; 'No US funds are involved.' [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- delivery lag] The missiles are yet to be manufactured and are not expected to be delivered until a couple of years into the 2030s, two people briefed on the decision told Reuters. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Zelenskyy, via Firstpost] Zelenskyy said late Friday on X that 'deliveries may begin ONLY IN A FEW YEARS' and asked US/European partners to give Ukraine stockpiled missiles now, to be replenished by this purchase later. [CONTEXT] Zelenskyy had said Kyiv waited almost a month for sign-off on critical missile supplies while Russia stepped up energy/civilian-infrastructure strikes; the Oct 29-30 barrage included 17 ballistic missiles overnight (Ukrinform, Zelenskyy nightly address) and the Dnipro station strike (14-15 dead).
sections.what_verified: State Department primary + Reuters (T1) + Ukrinform (T2, STATE UA). GMA carries the Reuters byline = same Reuters family, not counted separately. The Times (UK) and Firstpost have NO declared tier in the registry and are NOT counted; their delivery/production details are attributed only.
sections.what_disputed: Delivery is the dispute, not the approval: Reuters briefed sources (2030s) and Zelenskyy ('only in a few years') contradict any reading of this as near-term relief; the State Department statement gives no delivery estimate and the sale goes to Congress for review. Value discrepancy unresolved: a 24signal aggregator relay cites ABC Australia at $3bn vs the State Department $2.1bn -- the State Department figure governs; the aggregator is uncounted. Production context (attributed, uncounted): The Times cites the US DoD for ~600 Patriot missiles produced per year; Reuters notes July's up-to-$58.6bn Lockheed production contract and stockpile pressure from Iran-war munitions use.
sections.why_matters: 500 missiles approved -- but Kyiv will not see them for years: the approval vs delivery gap, with the counted $2.1bn / 500 / zero-US-funds figures and Zelenskyy's own 'only in a few years' warning.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Oct 30, absent from Oct 30/31 scans) -- US State Department approves possible $2.1bn sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 MSE interceptors to Ukraine, funded entirely by allies; Zelenskyy warns deliveries may begin only in a few years

totw_analysis: Our read: 500 missiles approved -- but Kyiv will not see them for years: the approval vs delivery gap, with the counted $2.1bn / 500 / zero-US-funds figures and Zelenskyy's own 'only in a few years' warning. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Relief or IOU? An approval Kyiv waited a month for -- but the missiles are not built yet, allies pay, and Congress still reviews: does this deter tonight's ballistic wave, or just promise the 2030s?
